#### Attachments

What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.
Images and other files can be attached too: pasted from the clipboard while the chat input has focus, dropped onto the chat input from the file manager, or chosen with a small ghost button with a paperclip icon, whose tooltip says "Attach files", on the tab row between the last tab and the help text, which opens the platform's file picker for any files, several at once. Pasting an image, or files copied in the file manager, attaches them rather than putting anything in the text, even when the clipboard holds text as well; every image and file on the clipboard is attached, and a clipboard with neither pastes its text as usual. Several files dropped or chosen at once are attached in their order, each on its own merits.
A file is attached as an image when its content is PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP, known by its content, not its name, and it is 5 MB or less, so the harness is given it as an image. Any other file is attached as a file, whatever it holds, text, code, a PDF, an archive, or an image in another format or larger than 5 MB, up to 25 MB; one larger is not attached, and a warning notification titled "Not attached" says it is too large. A folder dropped or chosen is not attached, the same notification saying folders can't be attached, and a file that can't be read is not attached, the same notification saying it couldn't be read, and why. Each file left out has its own notification, and the others are still attached.
Files can be dropped only on the chat input itself, its tabs, the attachments, and the text input; dropping them on the message list above it does nothing. While files are dragged over the chat input, its background is highlighted with the accent's fill, laid about a quarter of the way over it.
An attached image's row shows a small thumbnail, its file name, or "Pasted image" for one pasted, and its size in pixels, muted, with the same remove button; hovering the thumbnail shows the image larger, at most 320 pixels. An attached file's row shows an icon for its kind, a document, code, or a generic file, its file name, and its size, muted, as "14 KB" or "2.3 MB", with the same remove button. Images, files, and text are listed together in the order they were attached while the prompt is written. A prompt taken back into the input, as when a queued prompt is edited, lists its text first, then its images, then its files, each named by its saved file, a pasted one included.
Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps the attachments it was sent with.

##### Attached Text

A prompt with attached text gives the hidden anchor an attachedText

###### Property

a list with an item per attached piece of text, in the

order they were attached, keyed text1, text2, and so on. Since attached text is taken as it is, not as Piton, each is written as a multi-line escape block, as the userPrompt is, so nothing in it is interpolated or evaluated. A prompt with nothing attached has no attachedText property.

##### Attached Images

Each attached image is saved in the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, once the prompt is sent or queued, and a prompt with images gives the hidden anchor an attachedImages

###### Property

a list of the saved images' paths, from the project

directory, in the order they were attached, keyed image1, image2, and so on, each written as an escape block as attached text is. The same image attached twice is saved once but listed, and given to the harness, twice. The images themselves are never put into the compiled prompt as text. The preview draws its thumbnails from the images in memory, saving nothing.
The harness is given the images alongside the compiled prompt, in the way it takes images, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, in the order they were attached. A message sent to a running task can carry images the same way, and so can a question. A saved image that can't be found when the run starts fails it saying so, before anything is run.
Wherever an attached prompt is shown, in the latest task's header, among the previous tasks, in the questions of the Ask conversation, in the queue, and in the preview, its images are shown as thumbnails beneath the prompt as typed, between it and any slices, except in the latest task's header, where they come beneath the whole prompt, slices included. A message sent to a running task shows none in the task's output. The raw prompt lists their paths, as the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor) says. Clicking a thumbnail opens the image full size, in the platform's image viewer. Resending, sending to the other mode, and editing a queued prompt keep its images, and a Freeform prompt sends them as any other does.
What the harness receives is the compiled userPrompt followed by the attached text: a line reading "Attached text:", then each piece as a fenced code block, whose fence is longer than any run of backticks in the text itself. This is also the compiled prompt shown in the task's header.

##### Attached Files

Each attached file is saved in the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, in `.suspense/attachments/`, once the prompt is sent or queued, under its own name, in a folder named by the second it was saved and a short hash of its content, so the same file attached twice is saved once and two files of the same name never overwrite each other. A prompt with files gives the hidden anchor an attachedFiles property: a list of the saved files' paths, from the project directory, in the order they were attached, keyed file1, file2, and so on, each written as an escape block as attached text is. A file is saved as it was when attached; changing or deleting the original afterwards changes nothing.
The files themselves are never put into the compiled prompt. What the harness receives ends, after any attached text, with a line reading "Attached files:" and each file's path, from the project directory, one per line, with its original name and size, so the harness reads what it needs of them with its own tools. A run in a container is given each attached file of its prompt read only, at the same path under `/workspace`, mounted on its own, as a task's understanding file is, and nothing else of `.suspense/attachments/`. A saved file that can't be found when the run starts fails it, saying so, before anything is run.
Wherever an attached prompt is shown, its files are listed beneath its images, each as its row shows it, without the remove button; clicking one opens it as the [OpenFileScope](../../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) opens a file, or, for a file it can't show, in the platform's default application for it. A message sent to a running task, and a question, can carry files the same way. Resending, sending to the other mode, editing a queued prompt, and a chain's steps keep its files, and a Freeform prompt is given the "Attached files:" lines after its text as typed, since it is passed as typed otherwise.

##### New Conversation

The hidden anchor has a newConversation property, true or false, after the one recording whether it was sliced: for a queued task, whether it will start a new conversation rather than carry on its lane's; for the copy saved to the history, a task's or a question's, whether it did start one. A task starts a new conversation when it was marked to, as the session controls say, and also when there was none to carry on. Editing a queued prompt keeps what it says. A prompt saved by an earlier version, without it, still reads back, as carrying on the conversation.

content.text:
You can now attach any file to a prompt, not just images. The build is clean and all tests pass, including new ones for files, but I haven't tried it in the running app.

- **Attaching:** the button is now a paperclip, "Attach files", and opens a picker for any files. Dropping files or pasting them works the same way, including files copied in your file manager.
- **Images vs files:**
  - PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP of 5 MB or less still go to the harness as images.
  - Anything else up to 25 MB is attached as a file. That includes other image formats, larger images, and pasted images the harness can't take as images.
  - Folders, files over 25 MB and unreadable files are each refused with a "Not attached" notification.
- **Rows:** a file's row shows an icon for its kind (document, code or other), its name, its size such as "14 KB", and the remove button.
- **Saving:** on send or queue, files are saved under `.suspense/attachments/` in a folder named by the time and a hash of the content, so the same file is saved once. The prompt's hidden anchor lists them in a new `attachedFiles` property.
- **What the harness gets:** after any attached text, an "Attached files:" list with each file's path, name and size, never its contents. Freeform prompts get the same list after their text.
- **Containers:** container runs mount each attached file read only on its own. A run whose file has gone missing fails before it starts.
- **Showing and carrying:** files are listed under a prompt's images wherever it's shown. Clicking a text file opens it in the editor, and anything else opens in your system's default app. Files are kept by resends, sends to the other mode, edits of queued prompts, chain steps, questions and messages to a running task.

One gap from the spec: a message sent to a task already running in a container can name new files, but the container was set up when the task started, so those files aren't inside it.
